navigation._agent_profile_changed_20260826: WAS 'mount' (35 deg). The navmesh is built for the agents that actually use it, and nothing mounted exists in this project -- no mounts, no roads, no corridors. The consumers are the on-foot player and on-foot NPCs, which walk at 44.765 deg, engine-derived from the CharacterMovementComponent CDO. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE of the mount agent: the town's outer third was unreachable from its own plaza -- 19 of 60 street points in a different navmesh island, 0 failed projection, so navmesh existed under them and no path did. A basin town whose rim climbs 186.7 to 333 m is EXPECTED to fragment at 35 deg; that is what a basin is.
navigation._why_not_climb_70: REFUSED, deliberately. Recast at 70 deg pathfinds NPCs up cliff faces. Climb is the PLAYER's traversal reward, not an AI pathing surface. Do not fix navmesh fragmentation by raising this.
navigation._why_not_two_agents: A second +SupportedAgents entry creates a second navdata instance but CANNOT carry a different slope: AgentMaxSlope is not part of FNavDataConfig, it lives on the RecastNavMesh CLASS CONFIG, and setting it per-actor reverts via ARecastNavMesh::PostLoad when the voxel cache is on (RecastNavMesh.cpp:963-1015, already a REJECTED entry in R-NAVBUILD). Two agents would differ in radius/height/step and be identical in the one property that causes the fragmentation.

_mesh_provenance.why_not_hero_generated: /Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroFace and SKM_HeroBody are produced by scripts/build_hero_assets.py, which DUPLICATES the preview actor's transient meshes. That route is a DEAD END: duplicate_asset does not carry the reference skeleton, so the copies are degenerate -- every bone within 6 mm of one point. Measured with a negative control: assembled meshes read head_rise 160.6 cm and bone_z_spread 132-170 cm; the duplicated ones read 0.5 cm. A 320x separation.
